title: The Lesson I Learned From Hidden Motives — Proverbs 16:2
paragraphs: The Lesson I Learned From Hidden Motives — Proverbs 16:2
You can do the right thing for the wrong reason.
That’s the part that shook me.

Proverbs 16:2 says, “All a person’s ways seem pure to them, but motives are weighed by the Lord.” God is not impressed by polished appearances. He sees past the sermon, past the service, past the sacrifice, and looks straight into the engine room of the heart.
I learned that hidden motives are dangerous because they wear holy clothes.

You can help people and still crave applause.
You can serve in ministry and still be feeding pride.
You can post truth and still be chasing attention.
You can stay “obedient” and still be controlled by fear, not love.

Outwardly clean.
Inwardly divided.
And that’s where this verse cut me deep: sometimes the biggest deception is not what I hide from others. It is what I hide from myself.
But here’s what we miss: God exposes motives not to shame us, but to save us.

He does not uncover the heart to destroy the believer. He uncovers the heart to heal it. Jesus did this again and again. He confronted religious performance. He exposed false devotion. He peeled back the layers. Why? Because grace cannot heal the person we pretend to be. It heals the one we finally bring into the light.
That is the lesson.
Hidden motives will eventually poison what looks holy. But surrendered motives become worship.
So I have learned to pray differently now:
“Lord, not only examine what I do. Examine why I do it. Purify what people can see, and purify what only You can.”
Because in the end, God is not just after clean hands.
He wants a clean heart.

And the good news is this: in Christ, we do not have to fear exposure. We can repent. We can be made new. The blood of Jesus reaches deeper than behavior. It reaches motives, desires, loyalties, and secret ambitions. What shame tried to bury, grace can transform.
So bring your hidden motives to Jesus. Not tomorrow. Now.

He already sees.
And still He calls.
Still He forgives.
Still He restores.
He is purifying our hearts.
